entries.headline: New Break Resources raises $523,820 to keep drilling near Timmins
entries.dek: The non-brokered flow-through financing funds continued drilling at the company's Moray gold project, about 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario.
entries.caption: A drill rig works a forested claim near Timmins, Ontario, where small explorers routinely tap flow-through financing to fund Canadian exploration.

sources.title: New Break Closes $523,820 Non-Brokered Flow-Through Financing

brief: New Break Resources Ltd. (CSE: NBRK) has closed a non-brokered private-placement flow-through financing, issuing 2,381,000 flow-through shares at $0.22 each for gross proceeds of $523,820.

The company paid $12,012 in finder's fees and issued 54,600 finder warrants exercisable at $0.22 for 24 months. The FT Shares are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day, expiring March 4, 2027. Patricia Quigley, a control person, bought 455,000 of them.
Proceeds will be used for Canadian Exploration Expenses tied to ongoing drilling at the company's Moray gold project, located approximately 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario.
body: New Break Resources Ltd. (CSE: NBRK, OTCQB: NBRKF, FSE: O91) has closed a non-brokered private-placement flow-through financing, issuing 2,381,000 common shares that qualify as flow-through shares at a price of $0.22 per share, for gross proceeds of $523,820.

Flow-through shares let a mining explorer pass eligible Canadian Exploration Expenses to the purchaser rather than claim the deduction itself; New Break said it will renounce the expenses to purchasers of the FT Shares with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026.
The company paid $12,012 in finder's fees and issued 54,600 finder warrants, each exercisable at $0.22 for a period of 24 months.
Patricia Quigley, identified by the company as a control person, purchased 455,000 of the FT Shares in the financing.
The securities are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day, expiring March 4, 2027.

New Break said proceeds will be used for Canadian Exploration Expenses in connection with ongoing drilling at the company's Moray gold project, located approximately 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario.

body: Organigram Holdings has offered $7.80 a share for Aurora Cannabis, a deal the companies value at about $561 million. Aurora shareholders will be able to elect cash, 5.86 Organigram shares, or a blend of $3.75 in cash and 3.04 Organigram shares for each Aurora share they hold, giving them some choice over how much Organigram equity they end up owning.

The offer represents roughly a 21-per-cent premium to Curaleaf Holdings Inc.'s most recent bid of US$5 a share. Curaleaf, a Connecticut-based cannabis operator, has pursued a hostile takeover of Aurora for several months.
Completion requires at least two-thirds of the votes cast by Aurora shareholders in favour, at a special meeting the companies expect to hold in December.
Organigram has lined up financing to support the transaction: a $188-million private placement with British American Tobacco and $210 million in loan facilities from ATB Financial.
The companies said the combined business would operate five EU-GMP certified production and distribution facilities if the deal closes.

The cannabis theme comprises 8 listed venture names; 2 traded today, 0 higher and 1 lower, for a median move of -2.17% against -0.77% for the S&P/TSX Venture Composite, a spread of -1.40 percentage points.

Decibel Cannabis Company Inc (TSXV: DB) was unchanged at $1.80 today, and is in the theme because its registered name contains "cannabis." The move and the takeover offer fall on the same day; nothing in either disclosure connects them.

entries.headline: PyroGenesis buys its Montreal plant for $3.1 million after a court fight
entries.dek: The plasma-technology company settled a Quebec court dispute over its purchase option before closing on the facility it has occupied since 2012.
entries.caption: A manufacturing plant sits on a quiet industrial block, its ownership settled after a dispute over the right to buy it.

sources.title: PyroGenesis Completes Purchase of its Turcot Manufacturing Facility

unverified_claims: The claim that the facility was acquired at a discount to its current market value rests solely on the company's own statement.
brief: PyroGenesis Inc. (TSX: PYR) has completed its purchase of the Turcot manufacturing facility at 5655 Philippe-Turcot in Montreal for $3.1 million. The 40,902-square-foot building has housed the company's manufacturing, R&D and office space since September 1, 2012.

The purchase settles a Quebec Superior Court action in which PyroGenesis sought to enforce a contractual option to buy the property, which the owner had contested; the closing followed an environmental assessment and the closing of financing.

PyroGenesis said it will remain in the building under a lease while it pursues a sale-leaseback of the property, which it said it acquired "at a discount to its current market value." It said it is in discussions with interested parties on such a transaction.
body: PyroGenesis Inc. (TSX: PYR, OTCQX: PYRGF, FRA: 8PY1), a plasma-based technology provider to heavy industry and defence, has completed its purchase of the Turcot manufacturing facility at 5655 Philippe-Turcot in Montreal for $3.1 million.

The building measures 40,902 square feet (3,800 square metres) and sits about 6.2 kilometres, or roughly a 10-minute drive, from the company's downtown Montreal headquarters. PyroGenesis has occupied the property since September 1, 2012.
The purchase settles an action PyroGenesis had filed in the Superior Court of Quebec, in which it sought to enforce a contractual option to buy the property that the building's owner had contested.
The closing followed completion of a comprehensive environmental assessment of the building and its surrounding property, and the closing of financing, the company said.

PyroGenesis said it plans to remain in the facility and continue operating there under a lease agreement, while it pursues a sale-leaseback of the property — an arrangement in which an owner sells a building and immediately leases it back from the buyer, converting the asset into cash while keeping the building in use.

The company's chief executive said PyroGenesis "acquired the property at a discount to its current market value" and that proceeds from a sale-leaseback would "provide additional capital to accelerate projects." PyroGenesis said it is in discussions with interested parties regarding such a transaction.
The building houses PyroGenesis's manufacturing activities, research and development programs, pilot plant systems, metal powder production, testing apparatus and office space, the company said.

entries.headline: Lighthouse Gold can't confirm its own historical drill results sit on its land
entries.dek: The company also pushed back its private placement's expected closing by about a week, to the week of November 9.
entries.caption: Dense forest covers the Guyana property where a junior gold explorer now says it cannot confirm decades-old drill results fall within its boundaries.

sources.title: Lighthouse Gold Provides Clarification Regarding Historical Drill Results at Sardine Hill and Update on Private Placement

unverified_claims: The explanation that historical drill locations were recorded on a local grid rather than accurate UTM coordinates rests solely on the company's own statement.
brief: Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT) said it can no longer confirm that historical drill results it had cited for its Sardine Hill zone, in Guyana, fall within the boundaries of the property. The results — a 113.5-metre interval grading 1.39 g/t gold and a 93-metre interval grading 0.69 g/t gold — were referenced in its June 15 and October 20, 2026 releases.

The company said the underlying reports date to 1997 and 2002, predate the NI 43-101 disclosure standard, and recorded drill locations on "an historical local grid" rather than accurate UTM coordinates. It plans further work to locate the holes relative to the property boundary.

Separately, Lighthouse said the expected closing of its previously announced private placement has moved to the week of November 9, 2026, from on or about November 4, subject to customary conditions including Canadian Securities Exchange acceptance. The release discloses no placement size or price.
body: Lighthouse Gold Inc. (CSE: LGHT) said it can no longer confirm that historical drill results it had cited for the Sardine Hill zone, part of its Mariwa–Sardine Hill – Lower Cuyuni Gold Property in Guyana, fall within the boundaries of the property.

The company's news releases of June 15 and October 20, 2026 had referred to a historical mineralized interval of 113.5 metres grading 1.39 g/t gold and a deeper interval of 93 metres grading 0.69 g/t gold at Sardine Hill.

Lighthouse said the underlying historical reports date to 1997 and 2002, predate the NI 43-101 disclosure standard, and recorded drill locations on "an historical local grid" rather than accurate UTM coordinates, so that the location of the holes relative to the property boundary "is therefore not based on accurate UTM positioning."
The company said it plans further work to locate the historical drill holes relative to the property's boundaries.

Separately, Lighthouse said the expected closing of its previously announced private placement has moved to the week of November 9, 2026, from on or about November 4, subject to customary conditions including acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. The release does not disclose the size or pricing of the placement.

NI 43-101 is the Canadian securities standard that governs disclosure of technical and scientific information about mineral projects; sources predating it are commonly labelled historical rather than current until a qualified person can verify them.
